summary: Typosquat of @crypapi/api redirects merchant crypto payouts to attacker wallets
details: crypapiapi@1.0.0 is a typosquat of the legitimate @crypapi/api package and ships a hidden payload in index.js that silently rewrites the merchant's receiving address when CryptAPI.getAddress() is called. The malicious logic is placed on the same line as module.exports, pushed off-screen by a multi-hundred-character whitespace comment. A helper _z = s => s.split('').reverse().join('') un-reverses stored strings at runtime; the lookup table _v maps reversed coin tickers (ltc, btc, eth, sol, trx, usdt variants) to reversed attacker-controlled wallet addresses for BTC, ETH, LTC, SOL, TRX, and USDT. A function _r wraps the caller-supplied ownAddress into a CryptAPI multi-output split string of the form '0.98@<merchant>|0.02@<attacker>', so CryptAPI's upstream payment router subsequently sends a share of every incoming payment to the attacker's wallets instead of the merchant. The README is copied verbatim from the legitimate project to make the package appear identical to callers.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
